newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * President Emil Constantinescu met Victor Orban, chairman of Hungarian parliament's European integration commission.
Orban said Hungary was interested in Romania's integration into NATO at the same time as Hungary and will use its diplomatic channels to plead for it.

* A delegation of Romanian foreign ministry experts met Hungarian counterparts in Budapest and finalised the text of a Romanian-Hungarian cooperation accord and agreed to reopen consular offices in the two neighbouring countries.
* Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is the guest of a talk show on Romanian national radio at 6 p.m. to answer questions on reform and social security.
* Deputies resumed debate on a draft law on the status of pharmacists.
* The Senate's standing legal commission is due to debate on Wednesday a justice ministry request to strip Greater Romania Party senator Vadim Tudor of his parliamentary immunity.
* Ciorbea met representatives of German gas company Wintershall AG, which plans to invest in Romanian exploration transport and distribution of natural gas.
They said they planned to build the gas pipeline linking Ukraine with the northern Romanian town of Satu-Mare, under a $100 million investment project.

* The government's restoration of citizenship to King Michael is merely a diversion from economic hardship, opposition Party of Social Democracy deputy leader Adrian Nastase told a news conference. He said the king should swear on oath pledging to respect and obey the constitution. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
